findings.title: Every slice-design success criterion maps to at least one task
findings.description:
Cross-reference of the slice design's Success Criteria section against tasks:
- Indexed `[~]` → `status: 'deprecated'`, `isChecked: false`, description captured → Tasks 2, 3, 5.
- Unindexed form equivalence → Tasks 2, 3, 5.
- `totalSlices` includes / `completedSlices` counts deprecated as resolved → Tasks 4, 5.
- `cf list slices` renders `⊘ deprecated`, never `← next` → Tasks 9, 10 (rendering itself is already handled at `packages/cli/src/output/entryStatusDisplay.ts:17-19`, so asserting the derived status is sufficient).
- `cf next` / `findFirstNotCompleteEntry` skip → Task 11.
- `ConsistencyChecker` false-positive avoidance → Task 12.
- `[ ]`/`[x]`/`[X]` byte-identical regression → Task 5.
No task fails to trace back to a success criterion, no circular or violated dependencies (Task 1 before 2–3 is deliberately test-first; `dependencies: [910]` matches the design), and no load-test/CI item is required because the design restates no NFR.

findings.title: Task 1 mutates a shared fixture whose blast radius the breakdown does not account for
findings.description:
Task 1 adds one indexed and one unindexed `[~]` line to `sample-slice-plan.md`, which is consumed by five other test files. Task 5 only plans to update the `totalSlices`/`completedSlices` assertion (`slicePlanParser.test.ts:44`). Two consequences are unaddressed:
1. The new *unindexed* line enters `parseSlicePlan()`'s unindexed branch with no prior unindexed match in that fixture, so `unindexedCounter` yields `index: 1` and the index-ascending sort (`slicePlanParser.ts`, `entries.sort((a, b) => a.index - b.index)`) puts it **first**. That breaks the pre-existing exact-shape assertions `slicePlanParser.test.ts:12` (`entries[0]` → index 101) and `:22` (`entries[2]` → index 103), and contradicts the task's stated expectation that lengths/indices shift only by "two new fixture entries alongside the existing 5".
2. `slicePlanParser.test.ts:126` ("tags every entry indexSource: 'explicit' when the plan uses only the indexed format") and `ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:52` (`expect(result.totalSlices).toBe(5)`) also fail; neither is mentioned in Task 5, whose stated success criterion is scoped to `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test -- slicePlanParser` only.
The slice design explicitly permits the alternative ("extend the existing `sample-slice-plan.md` fixture **or add a sibling fixture**"). Put the `[~]` lines in a new sibling fixture (e.g. `deprecated-slice-plan.md`) so the shared fixture's five consumers are untouched, or enumerate the four affected assertions as explicit Task 5 steps.

findings.title: Task 9's `derivedStatus` initializer change is a no-op with an incorrect rationale
findings.description: Task 9 justifies its second edit — the initializer at `slice.ts:91` (`entry.isChecked ? STATUS.Complete : STATUS.NotStarted`) — by claiming that "a filesystem error would incorrectly report it as `not-started` instead of `deprecated`". That is not what the code does: every path through the `try` assigns `derivedStatus` (lines 122 or 124), and any throw — including `detectDocuments` failing — lands in `catch { derivedStatus = 'degraded'; }` (lines 125–127). The initializer value can never be observed, so the proposed change alters nothing while attributing a bug to the code that does not exist. Either drop this sub-step, or (if the fallback is being made robust for some future refactor) state that intent without the incorrect failure claim.

findings.title: Task 12 cannot verify its success criterion in the harness it targets
findings.description: Task 12 places the `plan-status-vs-entries` test in `ConsistencyChecker.test.ts`, whose harness mocks both `node:fs/promises` (module-scope `vi.mock` providing only `readdir`) and `parseSlicePlan` via `makeMockIntrospector` — the checker under test consumes only those mocks. `rulePlanStatusVsEntries` (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:726`) reads nothing but `completedSlices`/`totalSlices`, which a mock supplies verbatim, so the test as described ("a slice plan with frontmatter `status: complete` where every entry is either `[x]` or `[~]`") passes identically before and after Task 4's arithmetic change. It therefore does not demonstrate the slice design's success criterion ("`plan-status-vs-entries` … do not false-positive when … the only non-checked entry is a `[~]` deprecated one"). Make the task state the hand-constructed `SlicePlanResult` counts explicitly as the real parser produces them (with a cross-reference to Task 4), or move the end-to-end check to a real-filesystem harness such as the scratch-project pattern in `packages/cli/tests/commands/list-derived-status.test.ts`. Also note the design names `arch-status-vs-plans` alongside `plan-status-vs-entries`; both share the same `allComplete` arithmetic, so say explicitly whether the one case is accepted as covering both.

findings.title: Tasks 2–4 are granular enough to merge
findings.description: Tasks 2, 3 and 4 are each a 1–3 line edit inside the same `parseSlicePlan()` function, share a single test task (5) and a single `**Commit**:` marker, with no verification between them. Merging them into one "parse `[~]` as a deprecated plan entry" task would read cleanly and lose nothing; keeping them split is acceptable but adds no reviewable boundary.

findings.title: Task 10's commit lands Task 8's core change before its test exists
findings.description: Task 10's `feat(core,cli): thread plan-line deprecated status through resolveEntryStatus and cf list slices` commits Task 8's `WorkflowNavigator.resolveEntryStatus` change, but the only test for that core path is Task 11, which comes after. The CLI test in Task 10 exercises `slice.ts`'s inline duplicate, not `resolveEntryStatus`. Swapping Tasks 10 and 11 (or re-scoping the commit to the CLI change only) would keep each commit marker at a point where the code it introduces is covered.

findings.title: Plan-only entries in `ProjectModelBuilder` will not report `deprecated`
findings.description: `buildModel()` fills planned-but-unwritten slices with `deriveEntryStatus({ isChecked: entry.isChecked })` (and, in the plan-only initiative loop, with raw `entry.status`). With Task 4 adding fallback resolution elsewhere, a `[~]` plan line will still surface as `not-started` in model-driven output (e.g. the `archListFromModel` path). This is outside the slice design's stated Scope and outside every success criterion, so no action is required — recorded only so the divergence from the `Σ` deprecated rendering in `cf list slices` is a known, deliberate boundary rather than a surprise.

structured_findings.summary: Every slice-design success criterion maps to at least one task
Task 1 mutates a shared fixture whose blast radius the breakdown does not account for
Task 9's `derivedStatus` initializer change is a no-op with an incorrect rationale
Task 12 cannot verify its success criterion in the harness it targets
Tasks 2–4 are granular enough to merge
Task 10's commit lands Task 8's core change before its test exists
